note: Lifted semantic model, Cascade (IP/VPN) side. Home-grown, no standard vocabulary; same field conventions as the Meridian model. The two worlds are different domains and overlap only where a Cascade service rides a Meridian circuit as its underlay.

concepts.label: underlay
concepts.gloss: the transport circuit a service is bound to ride over — owned by the transport domain, consumed here

concepts.label: attachment
concepts.gloss: the logical point at which a service attaches to the customer site — where the IP service meets the customer router

concepts.label: rate
concepts.gloss: the committed information rate the service guarantees to the customer's traffic

concepts.label: latency
concepts.gloss: the latency commitment of the service, expressed as a named SLA tier rather than a raw number
concepts.example: SVC-42 is latency tier T2 (<= 8 ms)

concepts.label: protection
concepts.gloss: the resilience the service requires — that connectivity survive a failure in its transport path
concepts.example: SVC-42 must survive a single underlay path failure

concepts.label: grade
concepts.gloss: the IP class of service applied to the traffic — its scheduling and drop priority in the routers
concepts.example: SVC-42 traffic is gold class of service (low-latency queue)

concepts.label: vlan
concepts.gloss: the VLAN tag identifying the customer's traffic on an attachment — a purely IP/Ethernet object
concepts.example: C-VLAN 100 on the NY attachment of SVC-42

concepts.label: service
concepts.gloss: the end-to-end IP/VPN service delivered to the customer, riding a transport underlay; unknown to the transport domain, which sees only the circuit
concepts.example: SVC-42, a point-to-point IP service NY to FRA
